# fallkit — map your stack

> Paste the tools a company pays for (names only) and fallkit maps each one to a real, live estate build
> you could own and run yourself — or says honestly where there's no equivalent yet. It runs entirely in
> the browser against a fixed, reviewed table (never an AI guess); nothing leaves the page, and there is
> no pricing. Slice-zero of the auto-architect. Published by AI-Native Solutions.

## What it does

- Reads a list of tool names (e.g. Salesforce, Xero, DocuSign, Gmail, Aircall).
- Classifies each into one of four honest buckets:
  - MATCHED — a live build already does that tool's core job (names the repo, which is live now).
  - PARTIAL — a build covers part of it, with the gap named.
  - NONE — no equivalent exists yet, said plainly (e.g. voice agents, scheduling, payment processors).
  - UNKNOWN — the tool name wasn't recognised.
- Groups the result into eight company "seats" (Sales & CRM, Money, Legal, People, Work, Office, Overseer, Trust rail).
- States coverage as a count, never a price.
- Frames the NONE/UNKNOWN list as an honest build queue, not a hidden gap.

## Real builds it maps to (all live)

fallsalescrm, fallcrm, fallcall, fallpost (Sales & CRM) · fallaccount, fallinvoice (Money) · falljustice,
fallsignature (Legal) · fallhr, fallrecruit (People) · fallmail, fallscribe (Work) · glampos (Office) ·
agent-proof (Overseer) · the-wallet (Trust rail). A MATCH is a claim re-checkable by opening that one repo.

## Honesty notes

- Names only — never data, never an API key value. A live counter shows zero external requests.
- The map is fixed and reviewed, so the same list gives the same result on every machine.
- It maps and advises; it never runs a company, moves money, signs, or sends anything.
